Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with complaints consistent with cervical
whiplash injury. Over the course of seven visits, care followed a conventional and expected progression, beginning
with pain control, gentle range-of-motion exercises, and soft tissue management, then tapering in frequency as
symptoms improved. Physical examination revealed some objective findings, including reduced cervical range of
motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, which support the reported injury. Other neurological and orthopedic tests
were within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury to the cervical spine or surrounding area, and no earlier
complaints of this nature are documented in the record. The injury mechanism described is a plausible explanation for
the symptoms observed. Billing records reflect one charge per scheduled service with no duplicate or repeated
entries. At the most recent visit, the patient was improving and was advised to continue a home exercise program
with follow-up as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
